rules.rule: Present indicative has person-distinct singular and one form for allplural persons; weak preterite1/3sg coincide, 2sg adds -st to the selected1/3sg form, plural replaces its final e with on. No independent dual verb ending.

Selected present endings -e, -(e)st, -(e)ð, -að attach to the listed lexical stem. Gemination and i are retained in the 1sg/plural of short fręmman/nęrian types but absent in their 2/3sg. Longer diagnostic forms show the listed contraction and dental changes; do not infer each surface by merely appending the suffix to the infinitive.

rules.domain: hīeran, gefyllan and comparable lexical assignments
rules.rule: Class I -de with retained stem vowel; doubled consonant simplifies before the dental: fyllan→fylde, not fyllde. Short fręmman instead takes -ede and is a distinct lexical family.
ff/pp/ss dental preterites take -te and simplify gemination; tt type sęttan has sętte. Present2/3sg and past can coincide, but their analysis differs.

rules.domain: sęndan versus lǣdan; geręstan versus mētan
rules.rule: Consonant+d has sęnde versus vowel+d lǣdde; consonant+t has geręste versus vowel+t mētte. Preserve the lexical quantity; vowel length does not itself license deleting a dental.
Dental d becomes t after the relevant voiceless final: īecte. This differs from lexical irregular wyrc(e)an→worhte, which changes the stem and c to h.

The past is gierede. Cook allows present w retained or lost; the selected complete table retains w in1sg/plural and uses w-less full endings in2/3sg. This is disclosed selection, not allpresent w deletion.
Learn the diagnostic past stem with the lexeme: sęllan→sealde; gewyrcean→geworhte. Other §114 verbs are not silently assigned; the rule is not a free prediction from modern English.

gefręmman→gefręmede, ęfnan→ęfnede (source alternative ęfnde), nęrian→nęrede. lęcgan is an explicitly recorded exception (lęgde/lēde); no recall target. hyngran is impersonal and not substituted into personal sentences.
Use -ie,-ast,-að,-iað present; -ode,-odest,-odon selected past. Cook also prints -edon plural and other past-ending variants. -ian alone cannot distinguish II from short I; class is lexical.
Allfour survivors are separate complete systems: habban, libban, sęcgan, hycgan. Their present stem changes and selected past stems are not generated by the single lufian template.

Personal pronouns provide reflexive case forms. Selected productive frame geręstan + accusative self-coreferential pronoun; the same personal case form can otherwise refer to another entity. Form alone does not establish coreference.
Third-person genitives his/hiere/hiera are invariant. First/second genitive cells are not permission to use the corresponding inflecting possessive adjective without its later adjective paradigm.

Place ne immediately before the finite verb in the selected ordinary weak clauses. Complete nabban forms are recognition-only; ne+habban contraction is frequent, not compulsory. Negative copula and concord are not assigned.

teaching_boundaries: No source numbered Cook exercise is assigned by this audit.

Full12 finite cells are stored even when a learner table combines allplural persons and past1/3sg. Dual pronoun subjects use corresponding plural verb forms; no separate dual finite endings are invented.
Selected forms are a coherent bounded target, not a claim that unselected source variants are erroneous.
First/second-person genitives are recognition-only; mīn/ðīn/ūre/ēower/uncer/incer as agreeing possessive adjectives and sīn/self are deferred.
his/hiere/hiera are invariant possessives; possessive choice follows possessor, not possessed noun gender/number/case.
Simple productive negation uses ne with noncontracting weak verbs. nabban companion is recognition-only; copula contractions not taught. Source allows ne hæbbe as well as næbbe, etc.

Morphology does not grant new government/complement frames. īecan, gierwan, ęfnan, hycgan diagnostic paradigms can be practised as isolated form selection; ēhtan is an unassigned source comparison, with no new government rule assigned.
No passive/perfect/infinitive/subjunctive/imperative mastery follows from principal-part citations or reading support.
Prefixed reading verbs are separately checked lexemes; no general ge- aspect or sense rule.
